fields.AN_Notes: Edited volume (introduction, sixteen chapters, outlook) coded as one Work; codes collect what individual chapters carry as their own argument or result. Studientyp Theoretisch after the predominantly conceptual chapters; Plafky et al. report own usability tests and a focus group on an LLM case-note prototype, Holz et al. demonstrate classical NLP on a synthetic case, Schlomann draws on the KI-Alter field study. General_Guidance strategy: Plafky et al. instruct a local Mistral 7B with a fixed case-note structure (Wer, Wann, Wo, Grund, Ablauf, Diskussionsinhalte, Vereinbarungen, fachliche Interpretation, Entscheidung, naechster Termin; Tabelle 1), and testers ask for selectable templates per note type; Botzum et al. propose mandatory documentation of the prompts students used. AN_Prompting_Role: Learning_Content from Beranek (prompting as communicative competence), Recommended_Practice from Plafky et al. and Botzum et al., Object_of_Critique from Pelzl's analysis of prompting attacks as a manipulation practice. AN_Bias_Axes: Gender (Beranek's own example list, Schlomann's gendered digital divide), Race_Ethnicity (Steiner on the AFST and ethnically marginalised children), Disability (Steiner's chapter makes AI-related exclusion of disabled people its object and demands models that do not reinforce exclusion 'vor allem im Bereich Behinderung'), Age (Schlomann, age discrimination as own argument), Socioeconomic (editors' Allegheny poverty example, Schlomann on education), Language_Culture (Plafky et al., own observation that Swiss German dialect recognition depends on proximity to Standard German), Nationality_Migration (editors' bias-audit example and the Dutch child-benefit case). Sexual orientation appears only in enumerations. Intersectional not coded: the BIPoC-women facial-recognition result is cited from Buolamwini/Gebru without an own argument that depends on the combination. AN_Harm_Types: Exclusionary_Norms (editors: addressees deviate from the norm dominating internet training data), Erasure (Steiner: data selection and weighting under-represent marginalised discourses and groups; Tappe: AI-generated visual narratives decide which cultural references remain invisible), Disparate_Performance (own observation on dialect recognition, a quality difference between language varieties). Amazon hiring, Dutch child benefit, Allegheny risk scores, UNESCO images and Gender Shades are cited cases and stay uncoded under rule 1.4.1. AN_Mitigation_Status Proposed: training-data analysis, exclusion or synthetic data (Pre_Processing) and bias audit, diverse developer teams, ethics boards, human-in-the-loop and staff training (Organisational_Process) are recommended; the AFST evaluation reported by Steiner concerns a decision-support tool's side effect on ethnic disparities, not a tested bias mitigation. AN_Gender_Definition Absent and AN_Gender_Understanding Unclear: gender appears only in short discrimination examples, the cited gender gap of older women and men, and enumerations that also name LGBTQIA+ and queer people; no chapter determines gender, and these signals do not settle a binary or any other understanding. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit (Loehe; Dummann footnote 6; also Rottkemper). AN_Theory_Reference: Steiner frames under-representation and exclusion through a critical conception of inclusion and exclusion (Luhmann, Stichweh) with critical theory and Rojas' radical inclusion concept; Staub-Bernasconi, Media Equation and CASA frame ethics or communication, not gender or bias. Feministisch nein: no feminist theory or method and no structural gender critique.
